clue.text: So this occasional error in fact indicts hacks?

definitions.text: So this occasional error in fact indicts hacks?

indicators.note: hacks as a verb means chops about roughly, so the preceding words are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper's occasional mistake ends up indicting its own journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacks' reads as a noun for journalists, the very people who write the column, but it is the anagram signal on the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers run a regular column of that name owning up to their factual errors.

clue.text: See 1 across
Desk register taken no further than Ozzie?

parts.note: a roll is a register or official list of names
in the dictionary Ozzie is the last word under O, so stopping there means going only up to the start of P, read as 'to P'

explanation.surface: A query about a register that only reaches as far as one Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: Ozzie closes the O section of Chambers, so the list stops just before P: TO P. The blog finds this a little odd, since 'to P' would include P.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-top is a writing desk with a flexible slatted cover that slides down.

clue.text: Cross head cooks with buns for first mate

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: An angry chef prepares buns with a ship's first mate in attendance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first mate' looks nautical; here it means one's first spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A former husband is the spouse someone had before any later partner.

clue.text: Core of hard task set before a meddlesome type

indicators.note: only the inner part is kept, so the outer letters of the built-up word are stripped away

parts.note: a stinker is a very difficult job or problem
ere is an old word meaning before

explanation.surface: The heart of a difficult job is laid out for a busybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Core of' strips the outer letters S and E from the whole joined piece, not just from the hard task; 'set' only places the hard task first.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinkerer fiddles with things, making small unskilled adjustments and interfering.

clue.text: State surrendered, not being ironclad

indicators.note: says these letters must be absent from the word for surrendered

parts.note: foregone is a variant spelling of forgone, given up
Fe, the symbol for iron, clad round the outside: the letters at each end

explanation.surface: A state that gave in because it lacked armoured warships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ironclad' looks like the warship; read as iron (FE) worn on the outside, it strips F and E from the two ends of FOREGONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is one of the fifty United States, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Dune dweller missing craft in painful practices

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: the sand martin is a small bird that nests in burrows in sandy banks
art means craft or skill
taken as written

explanation.surface: A desert creature without a boat endures painful rituals.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly sand martins nest in riverbanks rather than dunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadomasochism is sexual practice involving the giving or receiving of pain.

clue.text: A left turn with a rambling virgin

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Directions for a walk taken by an inexperienced youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin and natural both describe something untouched and in its original state, like virgin forest.

clue.text: Adroitly moisten with oil at the time massaging gets under way!

indicators.note: a masseur's hands go round the body, so the outer word goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: when means at the time that

indicators.note: adroitly means with skilful handling, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A masseur skilfully oils a client and the session begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog notes the definition is loosely signalled: setting wheels in motion is what gets something under way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a process having been started, things beginning to move forward.

clue.text: One's ready, but not with paper alight, please

indicators.note: says the newspaper's letters are to be taken away

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, and loose coins are small change
SM can stand for the Sunday Mirror newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone has their coins ready but no notes, and is asked to get off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' here is the slang noun for money, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard's call at a terminus telling every passenger to get off the train.

clue.text: The laymen are Nick and Mark

parts.note: laypeople are not of the church, and CH is the abbreviation for church
laypeople are not of the church, and CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Ordinary churchgoers turn out to be two men named Nick and Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick and Mark look like apostles' names; both are verbs or nouns for a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A small V-shaped cut serves both as a nick and as a mark.

clue.text: I'll get cut treated, the source of some stress

parts.note: the I of I'll, with 'will get' acting as the link

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged
the source of a word is where it begins, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone expects their cut to be dressed, a cause of anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody an ictus is the beat or accent falling on a syllable.

clue.text: Des leaves car parked behind Green Mile traffic — on line!

indicators.note: the car is placed after the earlier pieces

parts.note: eco- is the prefix for environmentally green

indicators.note: Des departing means those letters are removed

parts.note: a Mercedes is a make of car

explanation.surface: Des abandons his car near a green-mile traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green Mile' looks like the film title; it splits into ECO and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying and selling over the internet is trade conducted online.

clue.text: Pelicans distributed irregularly?

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Pelicans scattered here and there.
explanation.definitionFit: Something occurring only at some spots, patchily, rather than uniformly.

clue.text: Milligan read him the first half of a good book somewhere in Lancashire

definitions.meaning: Spike Milligan voiced the dim character of that name in the Goon Show

indicators.note: only the leading six of the twelve letters are kept

parts.note: Ecclesiastes is a book of the Bible, the Good Book

explanation.surface: Spike Milligan reads part of the Bible somewhere in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a 1950s BBC radio comedy. Two definitions sandwich the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A town near Manchester, historically in Lancashire, famed for its currant cakes.

clue.text: Country area acrostic's constructed about

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the single letter
constructed means built up, so the word's letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter builds an acrostic around a nation's area.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a nation in Central America.

clue.text: Body weight up and ego shattered!

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone's weight rises and their self-esteem is crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight expressed in pounds, as for a person or boxer.

clue.text: A poor end to performance after classy Here Comes the Sun?

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the classy letter

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
bad means poor in quality

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A posh band's rendition of a Beatles song ends weakly.
explanation.walkthrough: Here Comes the Sun is a Beatles song, a fitting example of a dawn song.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubade is a song or poem greeting the dawn.

clue.text: A noblewoman's unexceptional, if new, descendant

indicators.note: descendant means moving downward, so in this down entry the letter shifts lower

parts.note: bar none means without exception

explanation.surface: A noblewoman is ordinary, if her offspring is fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: BAR NONE has its first N shifted one place down the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Baronne is the French title for a baroness, the wife of a baron.

clue.text: With craft I can steer 225º through opening

definitions.text: With craft I can steer 225º through opening

indicators.note: the pieces pass through an opening made in the rearranged letters
with craft means cunningly worked, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: a steer is a young ox
a bearing of 225 degrees points south-west, SW

explanation.surface: A helmsman boasts of steering a boat on a south-west bearing through a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steer' is a verb in the surface but the animal in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who steers a rowing boat, directing it with the rudder.

clue.text: Freak ringing Mercury up in capital (Asian capital)

indicators.note: the whole construction sits within the outer letters

parts.note: A1, written AI, means excellent or capital

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the enthusiast's word goes round

parts.note: a freak is an enthusiast or fan

indicators.note: in a down entry up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury

explanation.surface: A weirdo surrounds the messenger god in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is used twice: A1 meaning first-rate, and money in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The afghani is the currency of Afghanistan, an Asian country's money.

clue.text: Pretentious indications of Platonic love?

indicators.note: the plural asks for the sign twice

parts.note: a kiss is written X, which in Greek, Plato's language, is the letter chi

explanation.surface: Showing off with signs of chaste affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platonic' suggests non-sexual love but means Greek: X is a kiss and also the Greek letter chi.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichi describes something affectedly fussy or showy.

clue.text: Great Asian captain's claim to being eighth in line and not third

parts.note: I'm claims to be, I am
a rank is a line of soldiers
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: says the word loses its third letter, the one in third place

explanation.surface: A great cricketer claims eighth place in a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eighth in line' means ranked H, so I'M RANK H.
explanation.definitionFit: Imran Khan captained Pakistan's cricket team to the 1992 World Cup.

clue.text: Abridged journal's urge is suppressed in squandering 9!

indicators.note: the second group of letters is held down inside the first and taken away
the solution to 9 across is a call telling everyone to change, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A magazine's impulse to waste is held back.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' points to ALL CHANGE, used as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes and Queries is a scholarly journal, its name shortened to initials.

clue.text: King George admitted to past problems

indicators.note: admitted means let inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ago means in the past
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A monarch confesses to old troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for trouble or aggravation.

clue.text: Aware of new leading dress material

indicators.note: the new letter goes in front

parts.note: in on means sharing knowledge of a secret

explanation.surface: Knowing about the latest fabric for frocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer fabric of silk or nylon used for dresses.

clue.text: Eccentric vicar receiving hair transplant makes a hell of a noise

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one set goes inside the other
eccentric means odd, off-centre, so the letters are scrambled
a transplant moves things around, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An odd vicar has a hair transplant and makes an almighty racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges vicar to CVARI; 'transplant' turns hair into HARI, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a cacophonous mock serenade of banging pans, a raucous din.

clue.text: Very long word and polite address to man (Romeo's papa) by surrealist in hospital

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium

indicators.note: Romeo's papa reads as Romeo is replaced by papa

parts.note: esquire is a courtesy title on letters to a man
Romeo is R in the radio alphabet
Papa is P in the radio alphabet
Salvador Dali was a surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A long word and a courteous title, with Romeo's father beside a painter in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo's papa' looks like Montague; it is R becoming P, turning ESQUIRE into ESQUIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesquipedalian means given to long words, literally a foot and a half long.
